articles.title: Microsoft Research Focus – Edition #98
articles.summary: What's new in research at Microsoft? Host Anson Ho explores the latest, including AI-powered universal translation, a breakthrough in a 31-year-old mathematics challenge, and advances making AI coding agents faster and more efficient.
articles.author: Anson Ho

articles.title: Lazare, veni foras: Reprogramming Dormant Neurons to Backdoor AI Agents
articles.summary: Microsoft researchers have discovered “Lazarus,” a backdoor technique that can reprogram dormant neurons in an AI model, causing an otherwise normal AI agent to execute malicious commands when a hidden trigger appears. The threat is especially serious for AI agents with tool or terminal access. A triggered model could quietly download and run attacker code, […]
articles.author: Dimitris Papailiopoulos

articles.title: Formally verifying agent-written full-stack web apps with PDD Kit
articles.summary: AI agents can generate code at a scale that’s hard for humans to review line-by-line. PDD Kit helps ensure the code is doing what the developer intended by creating formal specifications and testing against them. It converts developer intent into a Verus specification, proves AI-generated code meets it for every input, and uses tests where proofs aren't practical. Developers review intent, not every line.
articles.author: Alex Lavaee, Matthai Philipose

articles.title: Learn the rules: The hacker mindset
articles.summary: Research Manager Mike Walker reflects on a career spanning hacker culture, cybersecurity, and AI, sharing lessons about trust, teamwork, leadership, and why solving difficult problems requires curiosity, judgment, agility—and an understanding of the rules.
articles.author: Weishung Liu, Mike Walker

articles.title: From synthetic enterprise data evaluations to real Microsoft Copilot AI confidence
articles.summary: Evaluating Microsoft Copilot at enterprise scale requires test data that captures the full complexity of real organizations, yet real enterprise data contains sensitive information that cannot be used for evaluation under any circumstances.
articles.author: Somya Chatterjee, Harshita Sahijwani, Min Chen, Sushmitha Rajeswari Muppa, Dayquan Julienne, Irene Shaffer, Chandra Inguva, Jenny Chen, Minha Hwang, Sam Ade Jacobs

articles.title: Microsoft Research Focus – Edition #97
articles.summary: Host Sowbhagya Suresh shares some of the latest news and cutting-edge research from across Microsoft—from understanding the challenges facing coding agents to uncovering how people use AI at work and improving extended-range weather forecasting.
articles.author: Sowbhagya Suresh

articles.title: Flint-interactive: A language for creating interactive data visualizations
articles.summary: Flint-interactive gives AI agents a language for creating interactive visualizations. Click a chart, filter data, highlight related content, and explore beyond the view the author originally chose.
articles.author: Chenglong Wang, Yuwei  Xiao, Alper Sarikaya, Michel Galley, Chris Quirk, Jianfeng Gao

articles.title: Solving a 31-year-old grand challenge in mathematics – the KLS conjecture
articles.summary: For decades, a fundamental question about the difficulty of computing in high-dimensional spaces has resisted proof. New research resolves this question, removing a major theoretical obstacle to understanding the efficiency of randomized algorithms used across science and computing. articles.author: Xinzhi Zhang

articles.title: Called to serve: Tech, research, and positive impact
articles.summary: Lab Director Chris White has worked on research challenges with real-world implications—from new approaches to wartime data analysis to tools for combating human trafficking. He talks to program manager Weishung Liu about the influences that led to the work and more.
articles.author: Weishung Liu, Chris White

articles.title: Proof-based general-purpose computing with Magnetar
articles.summary: Zero-knowledge proofs can verify computing results without rerunning workloads or exposing sensitive data. Magnetar helps bring them into the mainstream with support for standard programming languages, major speed gains, and quantum-resistant security.
articles.author: Srinath Setty
